implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.handle_events() maps arrow/WASD keys to Snake.set_direction() and Snake.move() updates direction accordingly.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake moves on a grid and updates board each tick
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.update() accumulates dt, calls step() which invokes Snake.move() and then Game.render() draws the board, snake and food each frame.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Food spawns at random free cells and never overlaps snake
implemented_requirements.evidence: Food.randomize_position() builds a list of free cells excluding snake_body and chooses a random one.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake grows when it eats food
implemented_requirements.evidence: In Game.step(), when snake head equals food.position, score is increased and self.snake.grow(1) is called.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends on self‑collision or boundary collision
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.step() checks self.snake.hits_boundary() and self.snake.hits_self(); if true, state becomes STATE_GAME_OVER.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Current score is displayed on the HUD
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._render_header() draws "Score: {self.score}   Best: {self.best_score}" at the top of the screen.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Multiple difficulty levels affect game speed
implemented_requirements.evidence: settings.DIFFICULTY_SETTINGS defines speeds; Game.__init__ uses the selected difficulty to set moves_per_second, influencing move_interval.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Menu for selecting difficulty before playing
implemented_requirements.evidence: menu.Menu displays options from settings.DIFFICULTY_SETTINGS and returns the chosen difficulty to main().

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete, playable classic Snake game. Directional controls, grid‑based movement, food spawning, growth, collision detection, scoring, and a difficulty selection menu are all present and wired together. The code appears syntactically correct and relies only on pygame, so it is likely to run as‑is. No major missing functionality or fatal bugs were found.
